correctness.rationale: The assigned package RESULT.md (blob b30a0245bb347e2d37ac105129393cb20bd3ea29) identifies the radius-one closed-ball nerve of H(n,q) as the union of closed Hamming neighborhood simplices. For centers distance 1 the intersection is their coordinate line; distance 2 yields two common intermediate vertices; all other intersections are empty. Any non-line face with >=3 vertices has unique center, so descending-dimension free-face collapses pairing F with F+center remove the higher faces. A second set of free-face collapses on each coordinate line leaves only corner triangles and line-fan triangles, all graph edges at Hamming distances 1 or 2. Every extra distance-two edge bounds a corner triangle and fundamental cycles of the Hamming graph are generated by triangles in coordinate lines and commuting-coordinate squares; those bound retained 2-cells. Hence the residual 2-complex is simply connected and Hurewicz/Whitehead yields the wedge of B(n,q) 2-spheres for all n,q>=3. Independent from-scratch finite enumeration and direct free-coface checks yielded for (3,3) initial 2889 faces, 1134 specified collapse pairs, residual f=(27,243,351), beta2=134; (2,3) initial 177, 45 pairs, residual f=(9,36,42), beta2=14. The finite data do not establish the universal quantification.

originality.rationale: PASS best of knowledge: the primary Adams–Shukla–Singh Theorem 4.1 covers the binary q=2 hypercubes; Matsushita Example 3.5 covers n=2 rook graphs and not arbitrary >=3 factors. A distinct published Resultary record supplies only the (3,3) ternary instance, which the assigned statement expressly excludes from its originality claim. None of the inspected sources implies the general all-parameter n>=3,q>=3 elementary-collapse classification; its proof treats coordinate lines and corners for genuinely multinary higher products. Searches are bounded and may miss alternate categorical-product independence-complex treatments.
